subproblem.title: Part (III): linearity of the Lipschitz push-forward in the current, from the reference sequences (supplied Step 8)
subproblem.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q and D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary; for a test form φ, dφ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q φ, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative φ; |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ; A_ρ := thickening ρ A; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞); a map g is proper on F if g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K. For g : ℝ^p → ℝ^q, ω ∈ D^j(ℝ^q), η ∈ D^j(ℝ^p) and A ⊆ ℝ^p, 'η is compatible with (g, ω) near A' means: there is an open N ⊇ A with η(x) = ω(g(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ g x) for all x ∈ N. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}), LipPF(X, G, S) means: for every sequence (G_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, every open O ⊇ spt X and every L ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, and G_n → G uniformly on O, and for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). Assume (RS): for all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r ∈ ℝ and F ⊆ ℝ^m such that r > 0, F is closed, G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and G is proper on F, there are C^∞ maps G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2}, and G_n proper on F for all sufficiently large n (this is the conclusion of the sibling reference_sequence). Then the following holds: (III) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X, X₁, X₂ ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r > 0, S, S₁, S₂ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) and a, a₁ ∈ ℝ such that G is Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X ∪ spt X₁), G⁻¹(K) ∩ (spt X ∪ spt X₁) is compact for every compact K, X₂(ω) = a·X(ω) + a₁·X₁(ω) for all ω, and LipPF(X, G, S), LipPF(X₁, G, S₁), LipPF(X₂, G, S₂): S₂(ω) = a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω) for all ω.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 8 of the supplied proof of lipschitz_pushforward. Assume (RS) and fix m, m′, k, X, X₁, X₂, G, Λ, r, S, S₁, S₂, a, a₁ as in (III).

1. (The common support.) F := spt X ∪ spt X₁ is closed (supports of currents on univ are closed). By part (3) of the reused support_lemmas (U := univ, which is open; Z := X₂, Z₁ := X, Z₂ := X₁, coefficients a, a₁; hypothesis X₂(ω) = a·X(ω) + a₁·X₁(ω) for all ω), spt X₂ ⊆ F.
2. (Reference sequence.) (RS) with this F (r > 0, F closed, G Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and proper on F) gives C^∞ maps G_n with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and x ∈ O_F := F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on O_F, and G_n proper on F for all large n. O_F is open and contains F ⊇ spt X, spt X₁, spt X₂ (r/2 > 0), so (G_n) with O_F and Λ is an admissible approximating sequence in LipPF(X, G, ·), LipPF(X₁, G, ·) and LipPF(X₂, G, ·) (the derivative bound holds for every n, in particular eventually).
3. (Compatible forms.) Fix ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}). For each n such that G_n is proper on F, the reused compatible_form (P := m, Q := m′, U := V := univ, A := F, f := G_n) gives η_n ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) and an open N_n ⊇ F with η_n(x) = ω(G_n x).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_n(x)) for x ∈ N_n; for the other n put η_n := 0. So for all large n, η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near F, hence near each of spt X, spt X₁ and spt X₂ (same N_n).
4. (Limits.) LipPF(X, G, S), LipPF(X₁, G, S₁) and LipPF(X₂, G, S₂), applied to (G_n), O_F, Λ, ω and (η_n), give X(η_n) → S(ω), X₁(η_n) → S₁(ω) and X₂(η_n) → S₂(ω). Since X₂(η_n) = a·X(η_n) + a₁·X₁(η_n) for every n, also X₂(η_n) → a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω). By uniqueness of limits in ℝ, S₂(ω) = a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω). As ω was arbitrary, this is the conclusion of (III). ∎
proof_key_steps: F := spt X ∪ spt X₁ is closed and contains spt X₂ (support_lemmas (3)).
(RS) for F gives one approximating sequence admissible for X, X₁ and X₂, and compatible_form gives one eventually compatible η_n near F.
The three LipPF limits and X₂(η_n) = aX(η_n) + a₁X₁(η_n) give S₂(ω) = aS(ω) + a₁S₁(ω).

audit.reason: The conclusion is exactly Part (III). The support lemma places all three supports in one closed union; RS and compatible_form provide a common approximation and test-form sequence. Passing the three LipPF limits through the given linear identity requires no unstated mass assumption.
